description: This false-colour satellite image depicts an artificial irrigation reservoir and its surrounding agricultural landscape in Sicily, Italy. The central feature is a large, multi-compartmented water body, rendered in dark blue, which is characteristic of a man-made structure used for irrigation. The uppermost and largest compartment of the reservoir shows mottled reddish-pink patterns, suggesting areas of shallow water with sediment or emergent vegetation. Below it, two smaller, distinct rectangular water bodies are uniformly dark blue. The surrounding area is dominated by agricultural fields, appearing as numerous rectangular parcels in varying shades of reddish-pink (indicating healthy vegetation) and light blue-green (possibly bare soil, different crop types, or harvested areas). Distinct linear features, resembling roads or irrigation channels, crisscross the agricultural fields. The image illustrates a typical Mediterranean agricultural setting with man-made water infrastructure. The credit is from Eurostat, with the acquisition year partially visible as "201[unreadable]".
